title: Weather and zero-shot models on GB electricity demand (pre-registered backtest)

primary_sources.paraphrase: Archived report (12 Nov 2026): three zero-shot models and a weekly-lag regression get the same ECMWF day-ahead weather for GB national demand over a 960-day backtest. Weather cut error for all four; the models' edge over the regression largely disappears. Plan, code and inputs were frozen on 10 Nov 2026, before scoring.

Repository for the study series (MIT). Holds plans, locks, code, scored outputs and both results notes; weights are loaded at pinned revisions, and the README states Chronos-2 is under Apache 2.0. The first study, without weather, put Chronos-2 at 0.928 of the regression's error.

Results note. Q1 (confirmatory): weather lowers every forecaster's error, ratios 0.658 to 0.941. Q3 (descriptive): with weather Chronos-2 is at 0.966 of the regression's error, Timestral 1.074, TimesFM 2.5 1.453. The regression also had calendar terms the models lacked; given them too (exploratory), Chronos-2 is at 0.903.

Analysis plan frozen at tag weather-plan (10 Nov 2026), written before any forecaster saw real weather. Only Q1 is confirmatory (four tests at 0.0125); the comparison with the regression (Q3) is an estimate with an interval, no test. Result sentences were written in advance.

Model card of the central model: 120M parameters, zero-shot, takes past and known-future covariates natively, runs on CPU. The repository's commit history dates the weights file to 30 Oct 2025; later commits change only the README.

claims.text: With the same weather, Chronos-2's mean daily error was 0.966 times the weekly-lag regression's (the best of the three models; a rough tie).
With the same weather, Timestral-209M's mean daily error was 1.074 times the regression's.
With the same weather, TimesFM 2.5's mean daily error was 1.453 times the regression's.
Weather lowered the regression's mean daily error to 0.658 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered Chronos-2's mean daily error to 0.683 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered Timestral-209M's mean daily error to 0.773 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered TimesFM 2.5's mean daily error to 0.941 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
On the 925 days that are not bank holidays or Christmas, Chronos-2 with weather was at 0.940 of the regression's error (exploratory, added after publication).
claims.dataset: GB national demand (INDO), half-hourly, ordinary days

claims.text: Given the regression's calendar as well as the weather, Chronos-2's error was 0.903 times the regression's (exploratory, added after publication).
Weather closed 456 MW of Chronos-2's gap to the system operator's own forecast, 62% of the gap; the operator still leads.
The plan, code and inputs were frozen and tagged before any model forecast demand with real weather, and the backtest was scored once.

relevance.rationale: Electric load at sub-daily resolution (GB national demand, half-hourly; ours is hourly zonal PJM load). Day-ahead, issued 09:30 the day before, against our week-ahead 168 h. Weather enters as a known-future input from archived forecasts as public at issue time, which matches our forecast regime; the study uses temperature, wind and solar where our spec requires temperature only.

checks.notes: pre_registered: the plan is dated at tag weather-plan (10 Nov 2026) and the results note says the backtest was scored once on 11 Nov; the tag time itself was not inspected, only the dates the plan and note state and the PLAN.md commit date GitHub shows. Only Q1 (weather helps each forecaster) was confirmatory; the tie with the regression (Q3) is a pre-specified estimate without a test, and E4/E5 were added after publication. training_overlap_risk is about our run: the Chronos-2 weights file was committed on 2025-10-30 (Hugging Face commit history), before our first scored week (2025-11-10), so all 52 weeks follow it. The study's own backtest does overlap the models' possible training period, which it states. independent_replication: one research call found no replication of the GB experiment; it named related Chronos-2 load studies (arXiv 2609.06656, 2604.28149) with mixed results, known here only from source snippets and not fetched. Central model: Chronos-2, the best model in the headline comparison; Timestral-209M and TimesFM 2.5 are the other two. Licence: Apache 2.0 for Chronos-2 comes from the study's README and the Chronos code repository; the licence tag on the model card was not in the fetched text. Not verified: the contents of the Zenodo archive (only the file listing was read), results.json, and the numbers against the scored outputs.

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: On target (electric load with forecast weather as a known-future input, against a lag regression given the same weather), with a public record, plan, code and results, and its headline comparison can be re-measured now with Chronos-2, which is in runnable_models. Evidence is moderate rather than strong because the tie with the regression is a descriptive estimate, not the confirmatory test, and the regression had calendar terms the models did not.
implementation_hint: Chronos-2 with temperature through models/chronos2.py (weights amazon/chronos-2, direct_adapter) against the temperature-only regression, forecast regime, per zone: this is the protocol's primary comparison. Secondary rows for the study's other models: mistralai/Timestral-209M with temperature and google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch univariate, both through models_ff/run_ff.py. The study used revision 29ec376 of amazon/chronos-2, half-hourly data, an eight-week context and three weather variables; ours is hourly, 168 h ahead, temperature only.
